newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Hanil limit-up on investment report.
newsitem.headline: Hanil limit-up on investment report.

text.p: Shares in Hanil Leasing went limit-up in Monday morning trading on a local news report U.S. General Electric Capital Corp was trying to buy a 31.5 percent stake in the South Korean company, brokers said.
Hanil rose 620 won to 8,420 at 0230 GMT with 164,840 shares changing hands.

The Seoul Economic Daily said GE Capital was negotiating with Tokai Bank Ltd of Japan to take over its stake in Hanil Leasing at between 70 billion won and 80 billion won. The Japanese bank is currently Hanil's second largest shareholder.
A Hanil Leasing spokesman said he was not aware of the negotiation.
Hanil Bank is the largest shareholder in the leasing company with a 32.84 percent stake.
Hanil Leasing was one of the most actively traded shares, A Daishin Securities broker said.
